issues.failure_explanation: For a regular zero hypersurface S inside Ω, a transverse coordinate is s=f, and the reciprocal potential behaves as 1/s. It is neither C² on Ω nor locally integrable across S: its positive and negative parts both have divergent spatial integrals. Every admissible φ maps Ω onto Ω, so composition cannot remove this singularity from the spatial cost. Consequently the prescribed barrier does not give the claimed real-valued functional or a legitimate application of its smooth first-variation calculation.

issues.overall_effect: The singular obstacle potential does not instantiate the optimal-control theory presented in the paper; the claimed barrier optimization is ill-defined.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In this paper we restrict to the case $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{3}$ with $\varphi$ being a volume-preserving diffeomorphism on $\Omega$, and with Jacobian having unit determinant.

issues.failure_explanation: Whenever the spatial cost is well-defined, volume preservation gives ∫ΩV(φ(X))dX=∫ΩV(x)dx for every admissible φ. Thus the potential adds a path-independent constant and cannot change the minimizers or select obstacle-avoiding trajectories. Equivalently, setting P=p−V in the displayed PDE gives ordinary incompressible Euler: the pressure absorbs the entire conservative force. The stated discrete Helmholtz projection likewise annihilates a compatible discrete gradient of V.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: First, we used finite differences to approximate the solution of the first equation in \eqref{mod:eulereq}
Using a small time step of $\Delta t = 1.5\times 10^{-3}$, we integrated the flow over $140$ steps.
The pressure $p$ is determined by the divergence-free (volume-preserving) constraint $\hbox{div}\,v=0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The procedure as written specifies projection after the integration, but no intermediate pressure solve or projection enforcing incompressibility. A final Helmholtz projection guarantees only a divergence-free output. It does not turn an unconstrained nonlinear evolution into the constrained one: for the advective operator N and Helmholtz projector P, generally PN(U)≠PN(PU). Consequently the missing timewise pressure constraint cannot be supplied retrospectively by projecting the final field.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, after the time integration stage is completed we projected our solution to a divergence free-vector field using the approach explained in the previous section.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify and use a pressure/projection solve within every time update, starting from divergence-free data, and recompute the evolution with that constrained scheme.
issues.overall_effect: The described computation does not establish a numerical solution of the coupled modified Euler system throughout the reported evolution; only the final divergence constraint is established.
issues.title: An after-integration projection does not enforce incompressible evolution
issues.why_classification: A contained time-stepping construction using the existing discrete operators can recover a comparable simulation, but an endpoint projection alone cannot supply the missing dynamics.
